title: Platformers
blurb: Crash and Spyro anchor a chapter of mascot platformers that helped define the PS1's identity, alongside a scrappy British entry that beat its own Japanese release to market.

games.title: Crash Bandicoot
games.blurb: The spin-attacking marsupial that became Sony's first mascot, built by Naughty Dog around aggressively tight level design and a signature save-crystal structure.

games.title: Crash Bandicoot 2: Cortex Strikes Back
games.blurb: A sequel that added the jet pack and a wider toolkit of moves, widely seen as tightening everything the original got right.

games.title: Crash Bandicoot 3: Warped
games.blurb: The trilogy's high point, breaking up its platforming with motorbike, jet-ski, and biplane stages for real variety between levels.

games.title: Spyro the Dragon
games.blurb: A fully explorable, seamless 3D hub-world structure was rare for its time, wrapped around Spyro's charm, gliding, and gem-collecting loop.

games.title: Spyro 2: Ripto's Rage
games.blurb: Released across Europe as Spyro 2: Gateway to Glimmer rather than Ripto's Rage — one of this collection's clearest title swaps — while adding swimming and new powered abilities to the original's formula.

games.title: Spyro: Year of the Dragon
games.blurb: The trilogy's closer, adding four extra playable characters alongside Spyro and pushing the series' draw distance and world size further than before.

games.title: Rayman
games.blurb: A hand-animated, limbless hero from French studio Ubi Soft, built around some of the most punishing platforming difficulty of the era.

games.title: Croc: Legend of the Gobbos
games.blurb: Released in the West months before its own Japanese release (where it carried the different title Croc! Pau Pau Island) — an unusually reversed rollout for the era — this British-developed mascot platformer was originally conceived as a Yoshi game before becoming its own IP.

games.title: Klonoa: Door to Phantomile
games.blurb: A 2.5D platformer blending flat side-scrolling movement with a fully 3D dreamlike world, built around a signature double-jump-off-enemies mechanic.

title: Action-Adventure
blurb: Lara Croft and Solid Snake anchor a chapter of genre-defining 3D action-adventure, including two titles built by British studios that became global landmarks in their own right.

games.title: Tomb Raider
games.blurb: A British-developed 3D adventure that made Lara Croft one of gaming's first true global icons, built around tank-control platforming and tomb-puzzle exploration.

games.title: Tomb Raider II
games.blurb: A more combat-focused, faster-paced sequel adding vehicles and a wider arsenal to the original's exploration formula.

games.title: Tomb Raider III
games.blurb: Lets players tackle its globe-spanning levels in almost any order, trading the earlier games' linear structure for open-ended choice.

games.title: Metal Gear Solid
games.blurb: Hideo Kojima's cinematic reinvention of stealth action, built around avoiding detection rather than confrontation and a script unusually invested in film-style pacing.

games.title: Oddworld: Abe's Oddysee
games.blurb: A puzzle-platformer with a genuinely strange tone, built around Abe's ability to possess enemies and a GameSpeak system for directing fellow slaves.

games.title: Oddworld: Abe's Exoddus
games.blurb: A direct sequel expanding the original's mechanics with new powers and a much larger, more varied set of environments.

games.title: MediEvil
games.blurb: A British-made gothic-horror-comedy platformer starring a resurrected, famously incompetent knight, with a tone unlike almost anything else on the console.

games.title: Alundra
games.blurb: A top-down action-adventure often compared to Zelda, built around genuinely difficult, physics-based puzzle design that outpaced its own commercial success.

title: Survival Horror
blurb: Resident Evil effectively invented the genre's console template here, in a chapter that also holds its most atmospheric psychological successor.

games.title: Resident Evil
games.blurb: Defined the survival-horror template almost single-handedly, pairing fixed camera angles and tank controls with deliberately scarce ammunition.

games.title: Resident Evil 2
games.blurb: Widely regarded as the series' peak on PS1, running two interlocking scenarios (Leon and Claire) through the same zombie-overrun police station.

games.title: Resident Evil 3: Nemesis
games.blurb: Introduces the Nemesis, a pursuing enemy that can appear almost anywhere in the game rather than staying confined to scripted encounters.

games.title: Silent Hill
games.blurb: Traded Resident Evil's B-movie zombies for genuine psychological dread, with the town's famous fog originally a technical workaround that became a defining artistic choice.

games.title: Dino Crisis
games.blurb: Essentially 'Resident Evil with dinosaurs,' built by much of the same team and swapping the undead for genuinely unpredictable predators.

games.title: Clock Tower
games.blurb: A point-and-click survival horror game built around evasion rather than combat, chased throughout by the unkillable Scissorman.

games.title: Parasite Eve
games.blurb: An unusual hybrid of turn-based RPG combat and survival horror, based on a Japanese novel about spontaneous human combustion and mitochondrial rebellion.

title: Role-Playing Adventures
blurb: The genre PS1 is remembered for above all else — Square and Konami's golden age, including several celebrated RPGs that, unusually, never made it to Europe at all.

games.title: Final Fantasy VII
games.blurb: The game most responsible for bringing console RPGs into the mainstream West, built around pre-rendered backgrounds and then-unprecedented CGI cutscenes.

games.title: Final Fantasy VIII
games.blurb: Trades the series' traditional leveling system for the Junction mechanic, tying stat growth directly to a much deeper magic system.

games.title: Final Fantasy IX
games.blurb: A deliberate return to the series' classic fantasy aesthetic after two increasingly futuristic entries, built as a love letter to its own earlier games.

games.title: Final Fantasy Tactics
games.blurb: A tactical-RPG spin-off with a surprisingly dense political plot, built on an isometric grid battle system that spawned its own sub-genre of imitators.

games.title: Xenogears
games.blurb: An ambitious blend of philosophical, Gnostic-influenced storytelling with giant-mech combat — one of the few major Squaresoft RPGs of the era that never received any European PS1 release at all.

games.title: Chrono Cross
games.blurb: A spiritual successor to Chrono Trigger with a completely different cast and setting, notable for a soundtrack widely considered one of the format's best.

games.title: Vagrant Story
games.blurb: A dense, mechanically deep action-RPG set entirely within one abandoned city, built around a weapon-crafting and armor-break system rarely attempted since.

games.title: Suikoden
games.blurb: Built around recruiting all 108 of the 'Stars of Destiny' into a growing castle headquarters, a collection hook the series became known for.

games.title: Suikoden II
games.blurb: A direct sequel widely regarded as one of the best RPGs of its generation — and, thanks to a small print run, now one of the most expensive PS1 discs to collect.

games.title: The Legend of Dragoon
games.blurb: A four-disc epic built around the Dragoon transformations its title characters can call on mid-battle, timed-hit combat layered on top of traditional turn-based structure.

games.title: Breath of Fire III
games.blurb: Follows a dragon-blooded protagonist who ages in real time across the story, with combat built around his ability to transform into different dragon forms.

games.title: Grandia
games.blurb: An early example of blending real-time movement with turn-based combat on the same battlefield, letting positioning interrupt enemy attacks directly.

title: Fighting
blurb: Tekken's rise to the genre's top tier happened here, alongside a one-hit-kill sword duelist that rejected nearly every convention of the genre around it.

games.title: Tekken
games.blurb: A launch-era 3D fighter built on genuinely fluid character movement, establishing the series' signature four-limb-independent control scheme.

games.title: Tekken 2
games.blurb: Expands the roster substantially and refines the original's combo system, widely seen as tightening everything the first game established.

games.title: Tekken 3
games.blurb: Often cited as the high point of the PS1 fighting genre, adding sidestepping and a noticeably faster, more fluid combat rhythm.

games.title: Street Fighter Alpha 3
games.blurb: Brings the arcade original's huge character roster and three selectable fighting styles (Ism system) to console with minimal compromise.

games.title: Bushido Blade
games.blurb: Rejects health bars entirely in favor of realistic sword combat where a single well-placed hit can end the match outright.

games.title: Soul Blade
games.blurb: Released in the West as Soul Blade rather than its Japanese title, Soul Edge, reportedly to avoid a trademark conflict — the European version also swapped one character's nunchaku for a censor-friendly staff.

games.title: Rival Schools: United by Fate
games.blurb: Sets its fighting-game roster inside rival Japanese high schools, with two-character tag teams and story-driven presentation unusual for the genre.

games.title: Bloody Roar
games.blurb: Lets fighters transform mid-match into beast forms with entirely different movesets, a gimmick that gave the series its own identity in a crowded genre.

title: Racing
blurb: Gran Turismo's arrival redefined what a racing sim could be on console, in a chapter also carrying two moody, electronic-music-scored British flagship titles.

games.title: Gran Turismo
games.blurb: Marketed as 'the real driving simulator,' its enormous, meticulously modeled car roster reset expectations for what a console racer could be.

games.title: Gran Turismo 2
games.blurb: Roughly doubles the original's car count and adds rally courses, becoming one of the best-selling PS1 games in the process.

games.title: Ridge Racer Type 4
games.blurb: An arcade racer built entirely around drift technique, wrapped in one of the console era's most distinctive anime-style intro sequences.

games.title: Wipeout
games.blurb: A British-developed anti-gravity racer whose licensed electronic soundtrack (Chemical Brothers, Orbital) helped define PS1's early cool-factor image in Europe.

games.title: Wipeout 2097
games.blurb: Released in North America as Wipeout XL rather than keeping the European title — one of the platform's clearer NA-side renames, running the opposite direction from most of this collection's title swaps.

games.title: Crash Team Racing
games.blurb: A mascot kart racer built to compete directly with Mario Kart, adding a full adventure mode with boss battles on top of standard cup racing.

games.title: Colin McRae Rally
games.blurb: A British-developed rally sim built around genuine surface-grip physics, launching a long-running franchise named for the real-world Scottish rally driver.

games.title: Destruction Derby
games.blurb: An early PS1 title built almost entirely around vehicle-damage physics, turning car-crushing itself into the actual objective rather than a side effect.

title: Sports
blurb: A chapter of arcade-leaning sports titles anchored by the direct ancestor of the Pro Evolution Soccer series, sold under two different names on either side of the Atlantic.

games.title: ISS Pro Evolution
games.blurb: Released across Europe under the fuller International Superstar Soccer Pro Evolution branding roughly a year before reaching North America at all under the shortened ISS name — the direct predecessor to the entire Pro Evolution Soccer series.

games.title: Actua Soccer
games.blurb: A British-developed early entry in 3D football sims, built to compete directly with FIFA's arcade-leaning presentation.

games.title: FIFA 98: Road to World Cup
games.blurb: Timed to that year's World Cup, adding every qualifying national team alongside the usual club rosters.

games.title: Hot Shots Golf
games.blurb: An arcade-accessible golf game built around a simple three-click swing meter, launching a long-running series sold in Europe as Everybody's Golf.

games.title: Tony Hawk's Pro Skater
games.blurb: Turned skateboarding into a combo-scoring arcade genre almost overnight, its soundtrack becoming as iconic as the gameplay itself.

games.title: NBA Jam Extreme
games.blurb: Leans fully into arcade excess — no fouls, exaggerated dunks, and an 'on fire' streak mechanic — over basketball simulation.

games.title: International Track & Field
games.blurb: A button-mashing multi-event Olympic compilation, known in Japan under the Hyper Olympic name its earlier arcade entries used.

title: Puzzle & Party
blurb: Point Blank's light-gun mini-games anchor a chapter that also holds one of the PS1's strangest rhythm curios — a game that took fifteen years to reach North America.

games.title: Tetris Plus
games.blurb: Adds a dedicated Puzzle mode with block-clearing objectives on top of the standard endless mode, aimed at Tetris veterans wanting a new challenge structure.

games.title: Bust-A-Move 2: Arcade Edition
games.blurb: A bubble-shooting puzzle sequel best known for its two-player versus mode, built on the same core aim-and-match mechanic as the arcade original.

games.title: Point Blank
games.blurb: A light-gun mini-game collection with an enormous arcade pedigree, built around dozens of short, escalating shooting-gallery challenges.

games.title: Intelligent Qube
games.blurb: Released across Europe as Kurushi, actually reaching PAL shelves ahead of its own North American release — a minimalist puzzle game about stopping advancing cube formations before they crush the player.

games.title: Devil Dice
games.blurb: A dice-matching puzzle-strategy hybrid that would later return, retooled, as the PS2's Bombastic — one of the more unusual puzzle concepts on the platform.

games.title: Vib-Ribbon
games.blurb: A minimalist wireframe rhythm game that generates its courses from whatever music CD is in the player's own console — and, unusually, never received a North American PS1 release at all, only reaching the region 15 years later via PS3.

title: Simulation & Strategy
blurb: British studios anchor this chapter almost entirely — Bullfrog and Team17's genre-founding console ports sit alongside a serious-toned tactical RPG.

games.title: Populous: The Beginning
games.blurb: A British-made reinvention of the god-game genre Bullfrog itself founded, moving from 2D terrain manipulation to a fully 3D world.

games.title: Command & Conquer: Red Alert
games.blurb: A console port of the PC real-time strategy hit, built around an alternate-history setting where Einstein erases Hitler from time entirely.

games.title: Worms Armageddon
games.blurb: A turn-based artillery-strategy classic from another British studio, built around an enormous, joke-filled arsenal of increasingly absurd weapons.

games.title: Harvest Moon: Back to Nature
games.blurb: A fully 3D take on the farming-sim formula, deepening the original series' day-and-season cycle with more detailed town and relationship systems.

games.title: Theme Hospital
games.blurb: A British hospital-management sim laced with dry humor, tasking players with treating patients suffering from deliberately absurd fictional illnesses.

games.title: Front Mission 3
games.blurb: The first Front Mission to reach the West at all, built around deep mecha customization and a story that branches based on an early player choice.

games.title: Vandal Hearts
games.blurb: A tactical RPG with a noticeably grimmer, war-drama tone than most of its genre peers, built on a hex-grid battle system.

title: Licensed & Movie Tie-ins
blurb: Die Hard Trilogy's three genres on one disc anchors a chapter of largely well-regarded licensed titles from an era before movie tie-ins had a reputation for being rushed.

games.title: South Park
games.blurb: A first-person shooter built entirely around the animated show's crude humor, using clay-animation-style character models to match the show's look.

games.title: Die Hard Trilogy
games.blurb: A British-developed anthology squeezing three separate genres — rail shooter, third-person action, and driving — onto one disc, each tied to a different film in the series.

games.title: Disney's Hercules Action Game
games.blurb: A British-developed licensed platformer tracking the film's story beats, mixing on-foot combat with several distinct minigame styles.

games.title: Small Soldiers
games.blurb: A licensed action game built around the film's toy-soldiers-come-to-life premise, letting players command a squad through household-scale battlefields.

games.title: Austin Powers: Oh, Behave!
games.blurb: A trivia-and-minigame party title built around the film's catchphrases and characters rather than a traditional action adaptation.

games.title: Spider-Man
games.blurb: A well-regarded web-slinging action game built with a genuine sense of verticality, later credited as one of the better licensed superhero games of its era.

title: Cult Classics & Deep Cuts
blurb: PaRappa the Rapper invented an entire genre here, in a chapter carrying the deepest run of confirmed Europe-skipping Square RPGs found in this project yet.

games.title: Jumping Flash!
games.blurb: One of the earliest true 3D platformers on any console, played from a first-person perspective as a robotic rabbit bouncing through vertically-stacked levels.

games.title: Einhänder
games.blurb: An unusually dark, mechanically demanding side-scrolling shooter from a studio mostly known for RPGs — one of several Square titles from this era that never received any European PS1 release.

games.title: PaRappa the Rapper
games.blurb: Effectively invented the modern rhythm-action genre, built around a flat, paper-cutout art style and call-and-response rap battles.

games.title: Um Jammer Lammy
games.blurb: A stylistic sequel to PaRappa swapping rapping for guitar riffs, starring a guitarist whose skill is inversely tied to how panicked she becomes.

games.title: Tail Concerto
games.blurb: An anthropomorphic-animal action-adventure that, unusually, reached a France-exclusive European release nearly a year before its own North American debut.

games.title: Azure Dreams
games.blurb: A hybrid of randomized dungeon-crawling and town-building, letting players raise monster allies that carry over between runs.

games.title: Brave Fencer Musashi
games.blurb: An action-RPG starring a sword-wielding hero summoned to save a kingdom on a strict in-game deadline — another Square RPG of this era that never made it to Europe on PS1.

games.title: Threads of Fate
games.blurb: Released in Japan as Dewprism, this action-RPG lets players replay its entire story from either of two different protagonists' perspectives — and, like several Square RPGs of the era, never received a European PS1 release.

games.title: Legend of Legaia
games.blurb: A turn-based RPG whose combat runs on a unique directional-input combo system, closer to a fighting game's move list than typical menu-driven battles.

title: Arcade Ports & Multiplayer Curios
blurb: The largest chapter in the collection, gathering vehicular-combat launch titles, British sci-fi flight sims, and party-focused multiplayer curios built around the console's four-player adapter.

games.title: Twisted Metal
games.blurb: A launch-era vehicular combat game pitting armed cars against each other in a demolition-derby-meets-deathmatch format.

games.title: Twisted Metal 2
games.blurb: A sequel expanding the roster and arenas considerably, widely considered the series' high point on PS1.

games.title: Ape Escape
games.blurb: The first game built specifically around the DualShock's analog sticks, tasking players with net-capturing escaped monkeys across time-travel-themed levels.

games.title: Bomberman
games.blurb: Brings the series' classic grid-based, four-player bomb-battle format to PS1 largely unchanged from its earlier console outings.

games.title: Bomberman Fantasy Race
games.blurb: A kart-racing spin-off starring the Bomberman cast, trading grid-based battles for lap-based races with bomb-throwing power-ups.

games.title: Micro Machines V3
games.blurb: A British-developed miniature-vehicle racer fitting up to eight players onto household-scale tracks — kitchen counters, garden hoses, and pool tables among them.

games.title: Rampage World Tour
games.blurb: A port of the giant-monster arcade brawler, letting up to three players smash city skylines as an oversized ape, lizard, or werewolf.

games.title: G-Police
games.blurb: A British-developed atmospheric flight-combat game set in a rain-soaked, cyberpunk-styled off-world colony, built around genuinely moody sci-fi world-building.

games.title: Colony Wars
games.blurb: A cinematic space-combat sim from the same British studio behind G-Police, built around branching missions that respond to whether the player wins or loses.

games.title: Jet Moto
games.blurb: A futuristic hover-bike racer built around aggressive, physics-heavy track design full of shortcuts and vertical drops.

games.title: Crash Bash
games.blurb: A Mario Party-style multiplayer spin-off built entirely around the Crash Bandicoot cast, trading platforming for competitive minigames.

games.title: WWF SmackDown!
games.blurb: Launched what would become a long-running wrestling series, moving beyond the earlier WWF console games toward a fuller, more simulation-leaning in-ring engine.

games.title: Duke Nukem: Time to Kill
games.blurb: Swaps the mainline series' first-person perspective for third-person, time-travel-themed levels — a deliberate departure from the main FPS games.
